overview: Guyana is a country on the north-east coast of South America. Its capital and largest city is Georgetown. Guyana was a British colony until 1966, and it is the only South American country where English is the official language. Since large offshore oil fields were discovered in 2015, its economy has grown extremely fast.

geography.text: Most people in Guyana live on a narrow coastal plain, much of it below sea level and protected by sea walls and canals. Inland, the country is covered by dense rainforest crossed by large rivers. Kaieteur Falls on the Potaro River is one of the most powerful single-drop waterfalls in the world.

history.text: The Dutch first colonised the area, and Britain took it in the early 1800s, creating British Guiana. After slavery ended, workers came from India, and today people of Indian and African descent make up most of the population. Guyana became independent in 1966, and the discovery of offshore oil in 2015 began a dramatic economic boom.

events.title: Dutch colonies
events.text: The Dutch set up plantations along the rivers.

events.title: Workers from India
events.text: The first indentured labourers arrive from India.

events.title: Oil discovered
events.text: Large offshore oil fields are found.

government.text: Guyana is a republic in which the President is head of both state and government. The National Assembly is elected every five years. It is the only South American country with English as its official language. Venezuela claims the western two-thirds of its territory, a dispute before the International Court of Justice.

economy.text: Guyana has had one of the fastest-growing economies in the world since oil production began offshore in 2019. Before that, sugar, rice, gold, bauxite and timber were the main exports.

culture.text: Guyana's people include descendants of enslaved Africans, indentured workers from India, Indigenous peoples and others. It is culturally part of the Caribbean and a member of CARICOM. Kaieteur Falls is one of the most powerful single-drop waterfalls in the world.

items.title: Kaieteur Falls
items.text: Water drops 226 metres in a single fall.

items.title: Phagwah and Mashramani
items.text: Hindu spring festival and Republic Day carnival.

sport.text: Cricket is Guyana's favourite sport, and it plays as part of the West Indies. Guyanese players have included Clive Lloyd, who captained the West Indies to World Cup wins in 1975 and 1979, and Shivnarine Chanderpaul.

items.title: Clive Lloyd
items.text: Captained the West Indies to two World Cup wins.
